title: Raspberry Thumbprint Cookies
changes_from_base: Seedless raspberry jam, warmed, as the filling, plus an optional lemon-icing drizzle.
summary: These raspberry thumbprint cookies follow the classic method, filled with warmed seedless raspberry jam instead of lemon curd and finished with an optional lemon-icing drizzle once cooled.
equipment: 2 large metal baking trays lined with baking paper
stand mixer or electric hand whisk
wooden spoon with a rounded 1.5 cm handle end, or a 1/2 teaspoon measure

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: about 1 tsp per cookie; warm briefly so it pipes or spoons smoothly

steps.title: Cream butter and sugar
steps.text: Beat the softened butter and caster sugar together on medium speed for 2-3 minutes, until pale and fluffy. This version follows the same creamed shortbread method as the classic thumbprint cookie, but swaps in warmed raspberry jam for the filling and adds an optional lemon drizzle at the end. Beat in the egg yolks, vanilla and salt until smooth.

steps.title: Mix in almonds and flour
steps.text: Mix in the ground almonds, then add the flour on low speed, stopping as soon as the dough comes together. With no egg white in the mix, the dough stays low in moisture, which is what lets it hold a deep well without spreading. Be careful not to overmix once the flour goes in, or the biscuits can turn out tough.

steps.title: Chill the dough
steps.text: Wrap the dough and chill for 1 hour. The chilled butter firms back up, helping the shaped biscuits keep their definition and their wells in the oven. Use this hour to get the oven heating and the jam ready to warm later.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: During the chill, heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) for at least 20 minutes, with a shelf in the middle. A properly preheated oven sets the biscuit edges quickly, which helps limit spreading. Line two large metal trays with baking paper ready for shaping.

steps.title: Shape and press wells
steps.text: Roll the dough into 20 g balls, space them 4 cm apart on the lined trays, and press a deep well into each with the rounded end of a spoon handle. Pinch together any cracked edges, since they can widen further as the biscuits bake. The deeper the well, the more jam each one will hold once filled.

steps.title: First bake and fill
steps.text: Bake for 10 minutes, until just set, then re-press any wells that have puffed up. Warm the raspberry jam briefly until it loosens and spoons smoothly, then fill each well — warm jam settles flat rather than sitting in a stiff dome. Fill them while the biscuits are still warm so the jam has time to set as they finish baking.

steps.title: Second bake
steps.text: Return the trays to the oven and bake for a further 6-8 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden. The jam will look glossy and slightly bubbled at this point, which shows it's hot enough to have set properly. Golden edges mean the shortbread base is fully cooked through.

steps.title: Cool carefully
steps.text: Leave the biscuits on the tray for 10 minutes, as both the biscuit and the jam filling will be very fragile and hot. Move them to a wire rack to cool completely before icing. Makes about 32 biscuits.

steps.title: Add the lemon drizzle
steps.text: Once the biscuits are fully cold, mix the icing sugar and lemon juice to a thick, flowing icing. Drizzle it over the top of each biscuit and leave to set for 30 minutes before serving or storing. The icing adds a sharp contrast to the sweetness of the jam.

tips: Warm the jam before filling — cold jam from the jar is stiff and won't settle flat into the well, leaving an uneven dome.
Chill the dough for the full hour; this is a common step to rush, but skipping it leads to flatter biscuits with shallow wells.
Only drizzle the icing once the biscuits are completely cold, or it will melt into the warm jam instead of setting on top.
Pinch cracked edges back together when pressing the wells to stop the jam leaking out during the second bake.
Use seedless raspberry jam for a smooth filling that sets glossy and even in the well.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature, in a single layer, for up to 5 days. Unfilled baked biscuits freeze for up to 3 months; thaw, then fill and ice before serving.
